content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm starting a new thread hoping to get assistance with establishing communication between a [product_name] base module and [product_name] software, as previous suggestions haven’t resolved my issue. Here’s the situation: I can set up communication between [product_name] software and one device, but I can't with another similar device, even though I’m using the exact same networking setup. My laptop connects via an ethernet/USB adapter, and I set its IP address to 192.168.0.1. Test 1: My first device uses IP 192.168.0.2, and an operator panel uses IP 192.168.0.3. I plug my laptop, the module, and the panel into an unmanaged switch and can successfully ping everything. In [product_name] software, once I start a new project and go online, two unknown devices appear. When I upload from both, they become active network members, and the module's program is uploaded—everything runs as expected. Test 2: Next, I replace the first device with another, setting the same IP. However, when I try the upload step, only the operator panel becomes active. The module, although identical in configuration and pingable, stays inactive. Both devices are similar except for input and operating voltages. Any insights into why the second module can't communicate with [product_name] software?
Could you provide the exact [article_no] for the device that can't communicate, and which version of the [product_name] software are you using?

The working device is [article_no] with firmware [version_no]. The device not communicating is [article_no] with firmware [version_no]. Both utilize the same Ethernet port. The [product_name] software is version [version_no] from 2020-09-21.

The latest [product_name] software is required to communicate with the current module ([article_no]). Updating to version [version_no] should resolve the issue. You can find the upgrade and installation instructions on the official website.
Also, check the official [company_name] page for instructions on upgrading firmware on the basic unit from [version_no] to [version_no].

That did it! I installed [product_name] software [version_no], and now it detects the module. It’s helpful knowing the part number indicates the module version. Thanks for the clear, prompt, and effective support. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The thread discusses difficulty communicating between [product_name] software and a [product_name] base module, specifically when using different versions of devices. The problem was due to incompatibility between software and device firmware. Upgrading the software aligned it with the newest module, resolving the communication issue. This case emphasizes the importance of verifying software and hardware compatibility and version requirements.
